title: Tours of Europe since 1973 and the Lucky Millinder concert in Nice
summary: His first European trip was with Milt Buckner; in 1976 he led a Lucky Millinder tribute at Carnegie Hall and Nice.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Hey, in recent years, you've been doing quite a bit of traveling in Europe. How did you like Europe and who did you play with over there, Panama?

Well, my first trip over there was with Milt Buckner, and Arnett Cobb, Tiny Grimes, and a bass player from France named Roland Lavesoir, and I was very much impressed with the people in Europe by the way they accepted jazz.

And I made quite a few friends over there. Especially, like, people in France, and I have been going back there since 1973, and in fact, I'm getting ready to go there now with my own band; I'm taking my band over there in January of 1979.
Great. Have you ever been over there before?

No, I always was with someone else. Well, yes, I did. At the Jazz Festival, I played the music of Lucky Millinder there, which was in 1976, and went over very big. In fact, it was the highlight of the festival in 1976 and we played with the New York Jazz Repertoire Company.
And I had done this concert before at Carnegie Hall.

With George Wein Williams and at the New Repertory York Jazz Repertoire Company, and it was a great sucess, and so it was repeated again in Nice. But that was the only time I had ever had a band of my own over there.
